item.description: ABC News’ Senior Political Correspondent Rachel Scott has the latest on the state of the races as voters head to the polls across the country.

item.description: There are key House and Senate races that could determine control of Congress.

item.title: High-stakes midterms are test for future of Congress and Trump's presidency
item.description: Here’s a look at some key Senate, House and gubernatorial races to watch that could help define the outcome of the 2026 midterm elections.

item.title: Senegal's opposition-dominated parliament rejects revised budget bill
item.description: Senegal's powerful opposition party Pastef, led by former presidential candidate Ousmane Sonko, on Tuesday rejected a revised version of the country's budget, leaving the west African nation's enormous budget hanging in the balance. The revised ‌budget is crucial ‌to the West African country sealing a new programme with the International Monetary Fund.

item.title: WATCH: New states in play as record gas prices hit on Election Day
item.description: ABC News’ Chief Washington Correspondent Jon Karl and Chief Business Correspondent Rebecca Jarvis break down why states in deep-red territory are in play and the state of the economy on Election Day.

item.title: Bomb threats reported on multiple flights
item.description: Bomb threats have been reported on multiple flights, forcing planes to make unplanned landings and airports to temporarily close.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir shares New Jersey students' determination in 100-Yard Food Drive Challenge
item.description: Students at Howell High School filled their football field with over a quarter million pounds of food for the nonprofit, Dermer Dreams. David Muir reports on the volunteers that delivered.

item.title: WATCH: Lucky fisherman catches fish worth $1M
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a mechanic in Australia whose life just changed by a fishing contest.

item.title: WATCH: Man complete 31,000-mile walk around the world after 28 years
item.description: A British adventurer who has been walking around the world for almost three decades returned to his childhood home Monday.

item.title: Airlines warn budget raid will drive up passenger fares
item.description: Britain's leading airlines have warned the government that a little-noticed budget measure risks pushing up airfares for passengers.

item.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as midterm elections start
item.description: The United States has conducted defensive strikes on some Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, a US official said Monday, on the eve of crucial midterm elections. The unpopular Iran war and the resulting impact on U.S. gasoline prices and other parts of the economy have been a vulnerability for Republicans as they try to keep control of Congress. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Oliver Farry has more.

item.title: French schools blockade resume on smaller scale as holidays end
item.description: Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France on Tuesday to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike later this week. FRANCE 24's Claire Paccalin reports from the ground.

item.title: Uganda withdraws its troops from Somalia as fight against rebels persists
item.description: Kampala announced on Monday it had begun pulling its troops out of Somalia. Uganda was the first country to send deployments to help Mogadishu when the African Union set up an international military mission in 2007 to battle al-Shabab extremist rebels. But what is prompting Kampala to withdraw its troops now, as the battle against the militants continues? FRANCE 24’s Georga Calvin Smith is joined by Horn of Africa geopolitical analyst Anwar Abdifatah Bashir.

item.title: South Africans demand security and basic services as they vote in local elections
item.description: High crime rates and a lack of basic services are causing concern among many of South Africa’s 29 million registered voters. Water shortages and unreliable electricity supplies have also become symbols of municipal failures, angering voters and eroding support for the ruling African National Congress. The municipal elections on November 4 will offer a glimpse into whether these frustrations are shifting political loyalties.

item.title: US midterm elections: Food stamp crisis a key campaign issue in Arizona
item.description: Arizona, a battleground state in the US midterm elections, is at the centre of a sweeping overhaul of America's social safety net. Since US President Donald Trump's tax and spending law passed last year, about half of the state's food stamp recipients have lost their benefits – the steepest drop in the country. State officials now admit that some of them are probably still eligible, but the errors have caused food insecurity to spike. The fallout has become a key issue on the campaign trail.

item.title: DR Congo opposition figure Prince Epenge arrested for spreading fake news
item.description: DR Congo senior opposition leader Prince Epenge has been arrested and transferred to prison. He is being held on charges of spreading fake news. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Kinshasa, Emmet Livingstone, has more.

item.title: Chadian farmers suffer from intensifying drought and take stock of their losses
item.description: In Chad, Wadi Fira is one of the two regions hardest hit by the drought. Just a few kilometres outside Biltine, the regional capital, farmers take stock of their devastating losses. FRANCE 24's Harold Girard reports.

item.title: Virgin Media O2 to cut thousands of jobs in bid to reduce costs
item.description: Virgin Media ‌O2 (VMO2) is set to cut thousands of jobs, as it looks to save around £300m through "a reduction in the size of the workforce".

item.title: Control of Congress is up for grabs. What's the math for Democrats and Republicans?
item.description: Republicans currently hold majorities in the House and Senate. How many seats must Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer flip to seize control of Congress?

item.title: These House races could determine which party is in control in the next Congress
item.description: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are on the ballot when voters head to the polls on Tuesday. Here are the races that ABC News rates as Tossup.

item.title: Death toll hits 29 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, with 48 still missing
item.description: Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, President Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections. (Image credit: Ukrainian Emergency Service)

item.title: Four types of House races to watch on election night to know how it might go
item.description: As polls close on Election Day and results start rolling in, these are some of the House races that will help explain how the midterms are unfolding. (Image credit: Ryan Murphy)

item.title: Review: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is superb, streamlined and safe
item.description: Nintendo's new Ocarina of Time remake enshrines its place in the gaming canon for generations to come. But despite its stupendous production values, the game left me feeling oddly bereft. (Image credit: Nintendo)

item.title: Dozens killed, dozens more missing after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site
item.description: The death toll from a Russian attack in southern Ukraine on a site where people had gathered to receive humanitarian aid rose to 29 on Tuesday, with 48 still missing, as a wave of overnight strikes targeted power plants across the country, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people. Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, triggering emergency power cuts, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an online post. FRANCE 24's Emmanuelle Chaze reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.

item.title: Americans to vote in US midterms: Trump's Republicans scramble to stop Democratic wave
item.description: Republicans made a final push to avoid a predicted thumping in the US midterm elections, as Democrats seek to win control of Congress. A Democratic-controlled House would impose the first real political constraints on President Donald Trump since he returned to office in 2025. Polls show the Republican to be the most unpopular president in modern US history. FRANCE 24 International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani reports from Washington, DC.

item.title: 'Hopefully we make history': El-Sayed fires up Michigan Democrats on eve of crucial US Senate race
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed, the doctor vying for a crucial US Senate seat for the Democrats, made his closing pitch to Michigan voters at the Majestic Theatre in Detroit, in one of America's poorest communities. The left-wing former medical administrator has drawn huge crowds at campaign rallies across Michigan with his promise to make healthcare free for all Americans. FRANCE 24's team reports from Michigan.

item.title: Cheese theft becomes rife among Europe's gangsters
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Tuesday, November 3: We look at reactions and analyses in Poland, where pro-European Prime Minister Donald Tusk is involved in a standoff with the nationalist president over the composition of the constitutional court. In other news, there's fresh outrage at big tech, after Google went rogue in Finland and cut down 250,000 trees for data centre projects. Finally, cheese is France's most stolen food product, and it's the stuff of cold, calculated crime.

item.title: Could Texas turn blue? Democrat James Talarico takes on Republican establishment
item.description: In a state that has long been a Republican stronghold, Democratic candidate for the US Senate, James Talaricois is carrying the hopes of what once seemed unlikely: Texas turning blue. The former schoolteacher and Presbyterian seminarian has been doing well in polls against Republican Ken Paxton, the longtime state attorney general whose legal troubles have cast a shadow over his campaign.

item.title: Californians vote on billionaire tax to replace federal cuts in healthcare funding
item.description: California could become the first US state to tax the net worth of billionaires Tuesday under a ballot measure that has divided liberal leaders nationally and triggered one of the most expensive ballot fights in state history as the ultra-rich scramble to figure out whether they would pay the tax or flee. Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the revenue dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare.

item.title: Unclear what comes next as US strikes Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The United States on Monday attacked Iran's Qeshm Island, the Wall Street Journal reported, even as President Donald Trump signaled progress in negotiations with Tehran to end the eight-month-old conflict. The Journal, citing unnamed US officials, described the strike against Qeshm, the the largest island in the Strait of Hormuz, as the latest of a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out against Iran in recent weeks.

item.title: Midterms: Trump uses final appeal to talk about troubled Reflecting Pool
item.description: In his final major speech before midterm elections in which polls but the Democrats well ahead of the Republican Party, Donald Trump on Monday spent more than 20 minutes discussing pipes, joints and caulking as he touted his troubled renovations to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington. To many critics, the renovations have become a symbol of government incompetence and misplaced priorities after delays caused by peeling paint and algae growth ‌that turned the pool’s waters green.

item.title: West Ham sack head coach Nuno Espirito Santo after poor start to season
item.description: West Ham have sacked head coach Nuno Espirito Santo after the club won just six out of 13 Championship games this season.

item.title: Spanish footballer dies after on-field collision
item.description: Tenerife football player Jesus de Miguel has died after an on-field collision in a match on Monday, his club have announced.

item.title: Despite attacks, Saudi Aramco posts 34% rise in net profits in latest quarter
item.description: Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil giant saw its profits rise to $36.25 billion in the third quarter, despite seeing its infrastructure and even headquarters targeted by Houthi rebels. Elevated oil prices have offset the supply disruption caused by the Iran war. Also in this edition: North Korea denies any involvement in the largest-ever crypto heist and we take a look at how Russia's strikes against Ukraine are destroying what's left of its economy.

item.title: How NPR makes race calls in the 2026 election
item.description: Race calls are a critical part of election night and NPR partners with the Associated Press to make those calls. Here's how we do it. (Image credit: Justin Sullivan)

item.title: It's Election Day. Control of Congress is on the line, and what else you need to know
item.description: There are a lot of variables for how things will go today. Results will start to come in at 6 p.m. ET in Kentucky and Indiana, and then it will be off to the races. (Image credit: Jon Cherry)

item.title: A new cold war: hackers target fridges across the globe
item.description: NPR investigated cyberattacks on the digital devices that control industrial refrigerators, revealing the extent to which operational technology is exposed to damage and disruption. (Image credit: Fred Tanneau)

item.title: From 'model minority' to target, anti-Indian hate on the rise
item.description: A massacre allegedly targeting Hindu Americans was recently thwarted, but researchers say it helps to illustrate a growing and increasingly mainstream hate directed at South Asians in the U.S. (Image credit: Laura Bargfeld)

item.title: 'Messy,' 'divided' and 'scary': swing voters rate the country ahead of Election Day
item.description: One last check in with the Swing Shift voters before Election Day. All of them voted for President Trump. Now, they're rating his presidency and deciding who to support when he's not on the ballot. (Image credit: Tara Anand for NPR)

item.title: Oxfam's Destroy and Rebuild Index: 'Wealthy minority of investors benefit from both sides of crisis'
item.description: The world's most vulnerable populations bear the brunt and the costs of the climate crisis, while the wealthy and powerful profit. Oxfam France’s Climate Inequality Advocacy Officer Selma Huart examines the relationship between concentrated wealth, unequal exposure to disasters and investors profiting from both polluting industries and reconstruction. “They are burning the planet, benefiting from it, but they are also benefiting from rebuilding,” she explains. Huart places redistribution at the centre of climate policy, calling for taxes on wealthy polluters to finance protection for vulnerable communities.

item.title: Israeli opposition unites behind Eisenkot as Netanyahu says voters chose him for PM
item.description: Israel's opposition is on Tuesday due to meet for the first time since last week's closely contested election in which neither Gadi Eisenkot's change bloc nor incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing alliance managed to win a majority in the Knesset. All parties in Eisenkot's camp have endorsed him to be the next prime minister, but the hot-button issue will be whether to unite with the Arab parties who made surprise gains in the vote.

item.title: WATCH: 5 people at Chili's in North Carolina suffer burns after margarita mix-up
item.description: Three customers and two employees at a Chili's restaurant suffered chemical burns after an employee mistakenly used a cleaning powder instead of sugar to make the drinks, health officials say.

item.title: PSG face Villarreal as they aim to keep Champions League top spot
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain are away to Villarreal on Matchday 4 of the Champions League. With three wins from three matches, PSG sit top of the table, whilst Villarreal are 19th.

item.title: Job satisfaction hits record low as men drive drop in people wanting full-time work
item.description: Men are driving a fall in appetite for full-time work, while job satisfaction has dropped to an all-time low, new research shows.

item.title: Cyber attacks affect UK meat processing industry, top security official says
item.description: Cyber attacks have affected the UK meat processing industry, a top security official has said in the wake of hacks that hit supermarkets across Europe.

item.title: US midterms live: East coast polling stations open for pivotal election
item.description: US voters head to the polls Tuesday for Midterm Election Day. Democrats are widely projected to retake control of the House, though control of the Senate remains up in the air. They will need to gain three seats in the House and four in the Senate to overtake the Republican majority. Losing either will affect President Donald Trump's ability to pass legislation and serve as a referendum on his second term. Follow our liveblog for all the latest.

item.title: CPJ: 'Attacks on journalists almost always precede attacks on other rights to broader population'
item.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Jodie Ginsberg, Chief Executive Officer of the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ). The killing of journalists is not simply an assault on those who report the news, explains Ginsberg. It is an attack on the public's right to know, on institutional accountability and, ultimately, on the democratic foundations of society. As the global death toll among media workers continues to rise, a deeper crisis is emerging: the normalization of harassment, intimidation and violence against journalists and the persistent failure to hold perpetrators accountable. “If killers of journalists are allowed to literally get away with murder, that creates the conditions in which we see more and more of those attacks,” warns Ginsberg.

item.title: US carries out 'limited strikes' on Qeshm Island in Iran
item.description: The US military has carried out "limited strikes" on Qeshm Island in Iran - hours before the midterms are due to take place.

item.title: British troops will be allowed to fire at Russian forces if attacked during multinational mission
item.description: British troops will be allowed to fire back at Russian forces if attacked as part of a multinational mission to secure any future peace in Ukraine, Western officials have said.

item.title: GOP touts Stevens endorsement while El-Sayed's campaign reports a record haul
item.description: As Republicans touted Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens' 11th-hour endorsement of GOP Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers, Democrats downplayed its impact.

item.title: Prepare for cyber attacks or face empty shelves, businesses told
item.description: Artificial intelligence is "helping to industrialise cyber attacks" and is "highly likely" to be used in attacks on Britain's critical national infrastructure by 2028, the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) has warned.

item.title: Woman stabbed while jogging in Brooklyn on life support: NYPD
item.description: The NYPD said the woman had "sustained multiple stab wounds to the neck."

item.title: How do midterm candidates plan to fight inflation? Economists evaluate proposals
item.description: Proposals include tax cuts and an end to the Iran war.

item.title: What you need to know about the Election Day Voter Poll
item.description: The Election Day Voter Poll helps answer the question of who won and why and explain what issues were important in the election.

item.title: WATCH: Seahawks inspire young leaders beyond the field
item.description: ABC News' Kayna Whitworth reports live from Lumen Field in Seattle on how the Seahawks are helping kids build leadership skills and pursue their dreams.

item.title: WATCH: Video of ICE agent apparently pointing gun in bystander's face during arrest
item.description: ICE is facing new scrutiny over a video that allegedly shows an ICE agent pointing a gun in the face of a bystander in California.

item.title: FIFA to share documents relating to World Cup sell-off plan
item.description: FIFA will give members of its ruling council access to some documents for the first time related to the World Cup sell-off, Sky News understands.

item.title: WATCH: A look at the state of the midterm races
item.description: ABC News' Senior Political Correspondent Rachel Scott breaks down the state of play as a new New York Times/Siena poll shows Democrats are gaining ground, slightly pulling ahead in key Senate races.

item.title: WATCH: Sisters go from lifesaving surgery to running a marathon
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to cancer survivor Kate Stevens, who received a bone marrow transplant from her sister and, around two decades later, ran a marathon with her.

item.title: 'Everything is destroyed': Hackers target refrigerators in new cyber attacks
item.description: Cyber hackers have targeted fridges and freezers in supermarkets in several European countries including Ireland – causing temperatures to increase and food to spoil.

item.title: Advocates rally voters after dozens of polling sites closed in 'swing' Texas county
item.description: Community and advocacy groups in Tarrant County, Texas, are rallying to get voters to the polls after officials shut down dozens of polling locations before the midterms.

item.title: WATCH: Thrilling finishes at NYC marathon
item.description: Sweden's Andreas Almgren won his first men's NYC marathon, and Kenya's Shelia Chepkirui won her second NYC marathon.

item.title: British backpackers in Australia could face changes to visa rules
item.description: British backpackers in Australia could be forced to spend more time in regional areas under proposed changes to the country's working holiday visa.

item.title: Suspected far-right activists from Britain 'with tear gas bombs' detained in France
item.description: Five suspected far-right activists from Britain were detained in northern France last Thursday, according to authorities.

item.title: Former Ireland European 1,500m champion dies at age of 34
item.description: Former European 1,500m champion Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34.

item.title: WATCH: The volunteers helping get the NYC marathon running
item.description: While the spotlight will be on the nearly 60,000 people running the course, they would not be there without the help of thousands of volunteers on the sidelines.

item.title: Election workers describe toll of DOJ threats in court filings
item.description: California election officials described the Trump administration’s legal threats as having consequences on their mental health, according to court papers.

item.title: States push back on Trump's noncitizen voting claims
item.description: The Trump administration has warned several states that their voter rolls include noncitizens, but many of those claims haven't held up to scrutiny.

item.title: Ahead of midterms, backlash grows over soaring electricity bills
item.description: Nationwide, electricity costs have spiked approximately 5% in the past year, government data shows.
